text:
tom: Quick sync: private on-prem cluster security checklist. Main concerns: (A) how keystore-agent talks to HSM/KMS (egress model), (B) least-priv RBAC for agent, (C) ensuring audit logs are tamper-evident when forwarded out. Anyone already had a hardened reference?

rachel: We have a lightweight pattern we've used: egress-proxy sidecar (envoy) + DNS allowlist in netpol, plus short-lived certs for agent->proxy mTLS. Netpol only permits pods with label `role=egress-proxy` to talk to 0.0.0.0/0 on 443; keystore-agent talks only to proxy on localhost. That avoids wide IP allowlists.

kevin: Example NetworkPolicy I used recently (deny by default, allow proxy):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: keystore-egress-via-proxy
  namespace: infra-keys
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: envoy-egress
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8443
```
Then Envoy sidecar has the config to talk to HSM endpoints with cert pinning.

anya: RBAC: do NOT give keystore-agent cluster-admin. Use a namespace-scoped Role with the minimal verbs. Example Role + RoleBinding: `secrets/get`, `configmaps/get` (for config with allowed key IDs), and `pods/exec` only if we need health debugging.

kevin: Sample Role:```yaml
kind: Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: keystore-agent-min
  namespace: infra-keys
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  resourceNames: ["keystore-creds", "keystore-tls"]
  verbs: ["get"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps"]
  resourceNames: ["keystore-allowlist"]
  verbs: ["get"]
```
and then bind to a ServiceAccount `sa-keystore-agent`. No cluster role.

rachel: On KMS side, bind the key policy to the OIDC subject of the ServiceAccount or to the specific mTLS CN presented by the envoy. That way even if someone steals the SA token, they still need the cert (mutual TLS) to reach HSM.

ops-bot: [automated] NOTE: Node egress gateway (jump-host) IPs: 198.51.100.10, 198.51.100.11. Add to SIEM allowlist.

anya: Audit-forwarding: we sign audit entries with an agent key and then forward over mTLS to Vector. Example envelope fields we use in JSON log (make sure fields are immutable): `ts`, `op`, `key_id`, `requestor_id`, `signature`. Use ed25519 for signing.

kevin: Example signed audit line (pseudo):
```
{"ts":"2024-11-01T12:34:56Z","op":"Decrypt","key_id":"projects/foo/keys/bar","requestor":"sa-keystore-agent@infra-keys","signature":"MEUCIQ..."}
```

rachel: For tamper-evidence we also store a rolling Merkle root every hour in an append-only store (s3 or internal object store), and mirror the root to SIEM. That helps for later integrity checks.

kevin: Vulnerability note: we saw advisory CVE-2024-3310 in the keystore-agent transport layer. Mitigation: (1) upgrade to 1.3.0, (2) enforce egress-proxy with TLS downscoping so agent cannot directly speak to KMS endpoints, (3) short token TTL. Who will take the patch?

anya: I'll own the patch and rotation steps. Plan: build patched image, run canary in isolated namespace with restrictive netpol and audit checks for 2 hours, then promote.

sec-bot: [automated] SEC-3250 opened for CVE-2024-3310 (severity: CRITICAL). Assignees: anya, kevin. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-3250

tom: Add gate checks: OPA/Gatekeeper validating webhook to ensure manifests don't include `hostNetwork: true` for keystore-agent or allow egress rules other than to `envoy-egress` for that namespace. That prevents accidental wide-open changes.

rachel: Good call. Also add an eBPF-based egress monitor (Falco or custom) on the jump-host to alert if a node makes unexpected outbound TLS connections to unusual ports.

kevin: Pre rollout tests I will run (commands):
- `kubectl -n infra-keys exec deploy/keystore-agent -- curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://localhost:8443/health`
- `openssl s_client -connect kube-egress:443 -servername kms.example -showcerts` to verify cert pins
- SIEM verification: check last-signed-audit: `aws s3 cp s3://audit-root/merkle-root-latest.txt - | sha256sum`

anya: Incident playbook additions: on detection of exploit attempt: 1) revoke SA tokens, 2) block egress from affected pods via netpol patch to deny all, 3) rotate keys that had decrypts in the last 48 hours, 4) collect forensics tarball from canary nodes.

ops-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: pipelines/keystore/patch-1755557777 -> infra-keys/canary at 2024-11-30T09:00Z. Will post success/failure.

tom: Thanks. Let's avoid long-running exceptions. If anyone has pre-existing tooling (Gatekeeper policies, envoy bootstrap) share snippets here.

rachel: Dropping envoy bootstrap snippet in ops-docs repo. Also adding the Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate PR shortly.

anya: Will execute the first step of rotation immediately after canary passes.
